The '''2023–24 La Liga''', also known as '''LaLiga EA Sports'''<ref>{{cite news |title=EA SPORTS & LaLiga Announce Expansive New Partnership With EA SPORTS FC as Title Sponsor of All LaLiga Competitions |url=https://news.ea.com/press-releases/press-releases-details/2022/EA-SPORTS--LaLiga-Announce-Expansive-New-Partnership-With-EA-SPORTS-FC-as-Title-Sponsor-of-All-LaLiga-Competitions/default.aspx |publisher=Electronic Arts |date=2 August 2022 |access-date=27 April 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=EA SPORTS FC will be the title sponsor of all LaLiga competitions |url=https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/ea-sports-fc-will-be-the-title-sponsor-of-all-laliga-competitions|publisher=La Liga |date=2 August 2022 |access-date=14 May 2023}}</ref> due to sponsorship reasons, was the 93rd season of [[La Liga]], Spain's premier football competition. It commenced on 11 August 2023 and ended on 26 May 2024. 
[[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] were the defending champions, having won their 27th title the previous season.

On 4 May 2024, [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] were officially confirmed as champions with four matches to spare following Barcelona's 4–2 defeat to [[Girona FC|Girona]], securing a record-extending 36th title.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c0x05j54l8wo|title=Real Madrid crowned champions after Barca's defeat at Girona|publisher=BBC Sport|date=4 May 2024|access-date=4 May 2024}}</ref>

===Promotion and relegation (pre-season)===
A total of twenty teams contested the league, including seventeen sides from the [[2022–23 La Liga|2022–23 season]] and three promoted from the [[2022–23 Segunda División]]. This included the two top teams from the Segunda División, and the winners of the [[2023 Segunda División play-offs|promotion play-offs]].

;Teams relegated to Segunda División
The first team to be relegated from La Liga were [[Elche CF|Elche]], after a 2–1 loss to [[UD Almería|Almería]] on 2 May 2023, ending their three-year stay in the top tier. The second team to be relegated was [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], after a 2–2 draw against [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] on 28 May 2023, ending their two-year stay in top tier. The third and final team relegated to Segunda was [[Real Valladolid CF|Valladolid]], after a 0–0 draw against [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] on 4 June 2023, ending their one year stay in top tier.

;Teams promoted from Segunda División
The first two teams to earn automatic promotion from Segunda División were [[Granada CF|Granada]] and [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]], who were first and second respectively. Granada returned to La Liga after a one-year absence, while Las Palmas came back after a five-year absence.<ref>{{Cite web |agency=Agence France-Presse |date=2023-05-27 |title=Granada win Spanish 2nd division, Las Palmas also promoted |url=https://www.thescore.com/esp_fed/news/2655177 |access-date=2024-06-25 |website=theScore.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Menzies |first=John |date=2023-05-28 |title=Granada and Las Palmas secure LaLiga promotion, four teams to fight it out in the play-offs |url=https://www.football-espana.net/2023/05/28/granada-and-las-palmas-secure-laliga-promotion-four-teams-to-fight-it-out-in-the-play-offs |access-date=2024-06-25 |website=Football España |language=en}}</ref> The third and final team to be promoted were [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]], after winning the play-off final against [[Levante UD|Levante]] on 17 June 2023, returning after a onе-year absence.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lowe |first=Sid |date=2023-06-18 |title=Alaves' playoff promotion is a barely believable true story |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37873858/alaves-playoff-promotion-barely-believable-true-story |access-date=2024-06-25 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Zamora Trophy===
